summary: Master of the Hauppauge estate at Smithtown and first cousin of John's 8th-great-grandfather James Smith; John's 1st cousin 10 times removed.
bio:
Daniel Smith, born in 1691, was John's 1st cousin 10 times removed and a first cousin of John's 8th-great-grandfather James Smith, whose land bordered his. When Smithtown was divided among Bull Smith's heirs, the Hauppauge land fell to Daniel and his sister Deborah; he bought out her share and left the estate to his sons Caleb and Joshua. On 10 April 1736 he received land on the right of his late father Daniel Smith, including 493 acres at the head of the river adjoining the Islip line, and his unexecuted will gave his fourth son Joshua the Hauppauge Neck, 893 acres bounded south by the Islip line, west by the river and north by the north-east branch.

He married Hannah Brewster (1698-1761), which is why the family name Joshua Brewster Smith arose; whether she belonged to the same Brewster family as John Thompson's supposed wife is unproven. Their children were Daniel (1720-1795), Obadiah (1722-1794), Caleb (1724-1800), Ruth (born 1726, who married Job Smith 2d), Deborah (born 1729, second wife of Epenetus Smith 1st), Joshua (born 1732), Mary (born 1735, who married Judge William Smith and was the mother of Senator and General John Smith) and Micah (born 1739). Through his son Obadiah he was the grandfather of Mary Smith, wife of the Culper spy Abraham Woodhull.

His second wife was Tabitha Floyd, sister of William Floyd, the signer of the Declaration of Independence; after Daniel's death on 13 January 1763 she married Daniel Reeve and died on 27 May 1812 aged 78.

researchNotes:
When the town was divided among Bull Smith's heirs, the Hauppauge land fell to Daniel 2d and his sister Deborah; he bought out her share and left it to sons Caleb and Joshua (Wood p. 25). On 10 Apr 1736 he received land 'on the right of his father Daniel Smith deceased', including 493 acres at the head of the river joining the Islip line (Pelletreau pp. 236, 248). His unexecuted will gives 'my fourth son Joshua' the Hauppauge Neck, 'south by Islip line, west by the river, north by the north east branch', 893 acres (pp. 359–363). Married Hannah Brewster (1698–1761) — hence the name Joshua Brewster Smith; whether she is of the same Brewster family as John Thompson's supposed wife is unproven. Grandfather of Sen. Gen. John Smith (via daughter Mary).

Pelletreau ([R4-S1]): born 1691, died 13 Jan 1763; children by Hannah Brewster: Daniel (1720-95), Obadiah (1722-94), Caleb (1724-1800), Ruth (b. 1726, m. Job Smith 2d), Deborah (b. 1729, 2nd wife of Epenetus Smith 1st), Joshua (b. 1732), Mary (b. 1735, m. Judge William Smith; mother of Senator John Smith) and Micah (b. 1739). His second wife was Tabitha Floyd, sister of the signer William Floyd; after his death she married Daniel Reeve and died 27 May 1812 aged 78. Through his son Obadiah he was grandfather of Mary Smith, wife of the Culper spymaster Abraham Woodhull.
